s: A complete universe for your phone: your home screen, plus about thirty tools, all running on the phone.
k: launcher overview welcome home
x: Dante OS replaces Android's home screen: your paged desktop, your dock, your app drawer, your widgets, your folders. On top of that it adds modules: firewall, DNS filter, network audit, processor and battery settings, encrypted files, SSH terminal, feed reader, music player, personal server monitoring… Almost everything happens on the phone: no mandatory account, no ads, no statistics. The core universe is free; Dante Pro, a one-time purchase, unlocks the advanced uses and lifts the limits. You do not "lose" anything by installing it: your applications, data and Android settings are still ther

t: The two modes: full or launcher only
s: With or without root. You choose, and you can change your mind at any time.
k: root magisk kernelsu without root full mode
x: Full mode (root): all of Dante OS. It needs a rooted phone (Magisk, Kitsune Mask or KernelSU). Dante can then set network rules, tune the processor and battery, read the sensors. A risk warning must be accepted. Launcher only (no root): no root command is ever run. You keep the desktop, the dock with zoom, the drawer, folders, Android widgets, icon packs, wallpaper, and the modules that do not need root: Files, SSH, News, Sonic, Notifications, Private Node, JSON tools, fingerprint Lock, Guide. In launcher-only mode, these modules are hidden: Firewall, DNS Filter, XRay, Governor and Battery Roo

t: Set Dante OS as your home screen (or go back)
s: So the Home button opens Dante, and how to get your old launcher back.
x: Dante's welcome offers to set Dante OS as the default launcher. If you refused or changed your mind, everything is set in Android.

s: Five minutes to settle in.
x: A simple sequence to make the phone yours.

s: Only once, when they are needed.

s: The menu for arranging everything.
k: menu gear button add organize customize arrange pages wallpaper
x: Tap the ⚙ button at the bottom right of the desktop: a menu opens at the bottom of the screen, with three tiles. The arrows at the top of the menu move from one desktop page to another. • Add: an app or a module, a Dante widget, an Android widget, placed on the page shown. • Organize: "Move" (drag widgets and pull their corners, then "Done"), "Arrange page" (everything lines up on the grid), "All pages" (the same everywhere; "Undo arrangement" appears right after), "Add page" (6 maximum) and "Delete page" (its items move to the other pages, nothing is erased). • Customize: Dante Engine, Icons,

Widgets are moved and resized from the desktop menu → "Organ

The folder shows a preview of what it holds. To give it its own icon: hold it and release to open its menu, "Change icon", then pick an image from the phone (PNG…) or an icon from a pack. x: A Dante widget shows a live measurement: processor, memory, battery, network, VPN, IP address, temperatures (root). An Android widget is one from one of your applications (weather, calendar…). x: When an application creates a shortcut (a web page, a file, a contact…), it appears on the desktop with its own icon, not the parent application's.

Tap the bar's time: the "Dante / Infos" popup opens. x: Bubbles flee your finger, bounce off each other and travel from page to page. Shapes: round, square, hexagon, heart, star, cloud; the size is adjustable. Pool mode: bubbles become balls on the shown page, and a black hole shows up that bends them. Your job is to sink them, against the clock.

No confirmation, so you don't lose a second: an effect swallows the screen, apps and background, and only the void remains. Your fingerprint (or code) puts everything back. It holds: after a restart, Dante comes back hidden. The home button leads back to the void, and incoming calls still show normally. s: A column of icons on the screen edge (a row at the top or bottom), with a magnifier when you slide over it.
k: dock magnifier badge icons column
x: At the top of the dock (or at the bottom, your choice): the shield, which folds the dock with one tap. Below: your sections, each with its title and its icons (apps and modules mixed). All the dock settings are in the desktop ⚙ button → "Customize" → "Dock". Tap an icon to open it. Slide your finger along the dock: the icon under your finger grows in a floating magnifier that also shows its name, and the magnifier shows the icon actually displayed (a pack's or an image of yours, not the original). The numbered badges on icons count the app's unread notifications (notification access is needed)

s: All the dock settings, in four tabs.
x: Desktop ⚙ button → "Customize" → "Dock": a panel opens next to the dock, which changes live while you adjust. • Style: the tint, the glass opacity, the icon size, the edge margin, and the Thin or Floating style. • Position: the screen edge, where the shield sits, and "More settings" for the height and free placement. • Effects: the fold effect, the folded shield effect, the speed and the auto fold. • Content: add an app or a module, a new section, a separator, show or hide names, and the shield's notification bubble.

s: Open, move, rename, change the icon, remove.
x: • Short tap: opens the app or module. • Long press without moving: the item's menu opens. It offers Rename, Change the icon, Put on the desktop (on the displayed page) and Remove from the dock. • Long press then drag vertically: you move the item within its section; release at the new place. Removing from the dock asks for confirmation: the app (or module) stays installed, it only disappears from the dock.

s: Organize the dock by theme.
x: Each section has a title (for example "Security", "System") and its own list of icons. A long press on the section header (next to the "+") opens its menu: rename the section, or delete it (with confirmation; apps stay installed). A short tap on the "+" adds an app or a module. Separators are simple spaces between two groups of icons. The separator's menu lets you delete it. "Clear the dock" (desktop ⚙ button → Customize → Backup → Advanced) removes all sections and icons at once, after confirmation.

s: One tap on the shield, at the top (or bottom) of the dock.
x: Tap the shield: the icons are sucked into it one by one, and only the Dante OS shield is left, on its line, with no tray behind it (the desktop is freed). A red sticker shows the total of the dock's notifications (up to 99+); it disappears once the dock is unfolded, each icon showing its own again. Tap the shield again: the dock unrolls downward like a tongue.

s: The edge, the shield, the height and free placement.
x: Dock panel → "Position" tab. The dock changes live as you adjust: • Edge: left, right, top or bottom. • Shield: at the top or bottom of a column dock; when folded, in place or in the middle. • "More settings": the maximum height (200 to 700 dp) and auto-scroll at the edge (the list scrolls by itself when your finger heads to its end). Icon size, opacity and edge margin are in the "Style" tab. Free placement (in "More settings"): turn it on to move the dock anywhere (long press on the dock, then drag). "Lock movement" avoids accidental moves, "Snap to edges" attracts the dock to the nearest edg

s: The dock's look and its effects.
x: Dock panel → "Style" tab: • Tint: a palette of colors for the dock glass. • Glass opacity: 10 to 100%. Icon size: 22 to 64 dp. Edge margin: 0 to 48 dp. • Style: Thin or Floating. "Effects" tab: • Fold effect: Tongue, Snake, Vacuum, Whip, Supernova, Teleport. • Folded shield effect: Lightning, Black hole, Fire, Magic, Force field, Ice, Glitch. • The "Dante" effects (Lock, Guardian) are reserved for Dante Pro. • Fold speed (50 to 200%) and auto fold (never, or after 3 to 30 seconds). Names next to the icons are shown or hidden in the "Content" tab.

s: Change the look of one icon or all of them.
x: • For the whole phone: Icon pack (desktop ⚙ button → Customize → Icons → Icon pack). Choose "Original icons" (those of each app) or an icon pack installed on your phone; the choice applies to the desktop and the dock. • For one icon: long press on the item → "Change the icon". You can take an icon from a pack, import an image from the phone (PNG, JPG or WebP, automatically reduced and cropped), or "Back to the original icon". The dock magnifier and the desktop always show the icon you chose.

s: Seven tiles, one page each.
x: Tap the ⚙ button at the bottom right of the desktop, then "Customize". Seven tiles: Dante Engine (the theme of the whole app), Icons, Wallpaper, Dock (the dock panel), Widgets, Notifications and Backup. Each opens its page; the back arrow returns to the menu.

s: An image of yours, blurred if you want, or a solid color.
x: • Background image: choose an image from your gallery. "Adjust position and zoom", framing "Fill the screen" or "Whole image", opacity slider, and "Blur the image" with a strength slider (icons and widgets stand out better). "Remove the image" goes back to the color. • Background color: four dark shades. • Maximum readability: a dark background with well-contrasted widgets, in one tap.

s: Size, number per row, names, shape and icon pack.
x: The Icons tile sets the desktop icons: size (70 to 130%), number per row (4 to 6: the more there are, the smaller they get), a dark card behind or bare icons, and the names under each icon. "Icon pack": "Original icons" or one of the icon packs installed on the phone (the ones you download like any app). The choice applies to all your apps, on the desktop and in the dock. "Icon shape": as the app (the phone's own), circle, square, rounded square, teardrop, hexagon, triangle, star, heart or flower, with a preview on your real apps. The app's drawing is cut cleanly into the shape; old single-ima

s: Background, size, grid, refresh rate.
x: Appearance: • Widget background: four dark shades, more or less transparent. • Transparent Android widgets: removes the background of your apps' ones (Dante's keep theirs). • Maximum size: compact or large. • Grid while moving: shows the desktop cells when you move a widget. Dante widgets (battery, network, temperatures…): • Update every 2, 5 or 8 seconds. The faster, the more it uses; widgets stop when the desktop is not shown. • Detailed widgets: more figures in each widget. • Listed temperatures: 3, 4 or 5.

s: Live measurements on your desktop.
k: telemetry widgets cpu ram battery network temperature gpu
x: Dante widgets show live: processor, memory, battery, network, VPN, IP address and, in full mode, temperatures, Adreno GPU (Snapdragon) and WireGuard state. Tapping a widget opens the detail and the module that goes with it. Page 1 of the desktop also shows, under the clock, the three small icons of the DNS filter, the firewall and WireGuard. Place them from the desktop ⚙ button → "Add" → "Dante", and set their rhythm in "Customize" → "Widgets".

s: The icons of apps that notify, next to the clock.
x: A row of icons (those of apps that have notifications, and the bell) shows in the bar, right next to the clock (under the bar on the right if there is no room, for example with a large font). Tap it to open the notifications bubble. You choose: Always, When there are notifications, or Never. Android's shade and banners are set in the Notifications module, ⋮ menu.

s: Your desktop backed up every day, and in a file to change phones.
x: "Back up now" keeps the dock, desktop, folders, widgets and wallpaper. An automatic backup is also made every day. "Your backups" keeps the last 10, the 3 automatic ones and the state before each restore: "Restore" goes back to one of them. To change phones: "Save to a file", then "Restore from a file" on the new one. Advanced: "Configuration as text" (the JSON to copy or paste) and "Clear the dock", which removes all sections and icons after confirmation. Back up first, so you can go back.

s: A swipe down from the top of the screen.
x: Swipe down from the top of the screen (within the first centimeters, even if you start on the clock or a badge): the "Controls" panel opens, wherever you are in Dante. At the top, Wi-Fi and mobile data. Below, "Within reach": Bluetooth, flashlight, location, Do not disturb, rotation, dark theme, hotspot, and in full mode DNS filter, firewall, WireGuard… "Customize", at the bottom, picks which ones. At the very bottom, brightness and volume.

s: It replaces Android's notification shade.
x: Notifications grouped by app, quick replies, actions, avatars, swipe to delete. A "Now playing" card gives the controls for the current music; a collapsible "Ongoing" section holds permanent notifications. The numbered badges on the dock count unread notifications per app.

s: Allow or block Internet for each app, depending on the network type.
k: iptables network wifi mobile data block internet app rule
x: For each installed application, you choose whether it may use Wi-Fi, mobile data, roaming, the local network and tethering. A game that does not need Internet can be cut off completely; an app that should only talk on Wi-Fi can be cut on mobile data. Dante sets its rules in the Android kernel with iptables and ip6tables (IPv4 and IPv6), in a chain of its own named DANTE_FW. There is no VPN: your real VPN stays free. A log keeps track of each rule application, and an alert warns you when a new app is installed.

s: Block ads, trackers and malicious sites without a VPN.
k: dns ads tracker adblock blocklist relay vpn dot doh bubble
x: Before reaching a server, an app asks for its address (a DNS request). The filter answers "this domain does not exist" for ads, trackers and malicious sites: the ad never loads. Other requests are passed on normally to your network's DNS servers (failing that Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Quad9 9.9.9.9 or Google 8.8.8.8). With root, the phone's DNS requests are redirected to a small relay inside Dante OS (DANTE_DNS iptables chains): no VPN, so your VPN stays free. IPv6 DNS is sent back to IPv4, which is filtered. If Dante OS stops, a safeguard removes the rules so you are never left without Internet.

s: Network diagnostics and statistics: interfaces, throughput, gateway, addresses.
x: A dashboard to understand the state of your connection: the active interface (Wi-Fi, data), your IP address, the gateway and the current throughput. This is the module to open when "Internet does not work": it helps see whether the problem comes from Wi-Fi, the gateway or DNS.

s: Per-app traffic audit: rates, connections, permissions, risk, alerts.
k: xray traffic audit rx tx anomalies ports firewall risk
x: XRay watches which applications communicate, how fast, with what level of risk, and explains it to you. It mixes live traffic, Android permissions, network connections and alert rules. It is not an antivirus: an alert is a reasoned signal, not proof of malware. Without root, XRay reads per-application rates (received RX, sent TX, live and cumulative). With root (ROOT badge), it also reads sockets, ports, connections and iptables rules. Depending on the device, it picks the right measurement source by itself; if your phone limits statistics without root, it shows N/A rather than a false 0. Valu

s: Processor profiles and heat protection.
k: cpu processor frequency heat temperature profile walt
x: Choose a profile: balanced, performance or economy. Dante then sets the processor's frequency limits. Heat protection automatically moves the phone to a more cautious profile when it exceeds a temperature threshold. Dante respects WALT (Qualcomm's load manager) and only touches speed limits, never the rest of the system.

s: Battery health, charge control, per-app consumption.
k: battery charge health cycles current
x: Shows the battery's real state read by the kernel: health, temperature, charge or discharge current. It also shows which apps consume the most, and lets you control charging on devices that allow it. Hibernation: on an app, "Hibernate app" cuts it off completely, without uninstalling it. It can no longer start, in the background or on a tap, and uses nothing. It appears in the "Hibernated apps" list, where "Wake app" restores it straight away. Only root allows this clean cut: Dante disables the app at system level, like the security freeze does. A simple power-saving list leaves the app free t

s: The phone's vital signs live: load, memory, temperatures, network.
x: The same tracking as the desktop widgets, full screen: processor load, frequencies, memory, battery, network rate, VPN, IP address. Without root, you get basic telemetry (battery, memory, network). With root come temperatures, the Adreno GPU (Snapdragon) and WireGuard state.

s: The log of Dante OS and its modules, with search and export.
x: It is a homemade logcat, readable on the phone. "Dante OS" shows what the modules do (firewall, DNS filter, XRay, SSH, news…), newest first, sorted by hour; "Android" shows Dante OS's own raw logcat, live. Android only lets an app read its own lines: other apps' logs are never read. Module events and Dante OS crashes are kept on the phone, even when the screen was closed: Android's logcat only keeps the last few minutes. No password, key, SSH command content or notification text is ever written there. The three counters (errors, warnings, info) act as filters: one tap keeps that level, a secon

s: The Dante OS dashboard: live measures, modules, options, and every Android setting sorted into families, with search.
x: A dashboard instead of a long list. At the top, "Live": battery, temperature, memory, storage, network, uptime and IP addresses. A tap opens the matching module. "Dante OS": one tile per module (DNS filter, firewall, Gateway, XRay, security, Private Node, governor, battery root) with its current state. "All modules" opens the full list. "Dante options": Dante's own switches (multitasking, bar in every app, watch, fingerprint lock) and the language. "Android" sorts Android's settings into twelve families: a family opens its settings flat, without stacked menus. The search at the top finds every

s: System health tests and read-only review of installed apps.
x: A series of checks on the phone's state, and a local review of installed apps: install source (store or outside a store), rare powers (installing other apps, displaying over others, starting at boot), sensitive accesses granted. It calmly flags what deserves a look. It is not an antivirus: a flagged app is not necessarily dangerous.

s: Read-only checks, with an alert at each change.
x: Every 30 minutes (if you enable monitoring), Dante looks at: accessibility services, apps holding root, Magisk modules, device administrators, installed certificates and ADB debugging. At each new change you get an alert. Nothing is modified: the module observes and warns.

s: File manager: phone, root, SSH, network, encrypted vaults.
k: files vault trash smb ftp sftp usb
x: Places: the ☰ button (or a swipe from the left edge) opens the phone, an SD card or plugged-in USB drive, the system (root), your bookmarks, your network shares and your SSH servers. Select: a long press selects an item; then each tap adds or removes. The bottom bar offers Copy, Cut, Share, Delete, and "More": rename, compress, encrypted vault, properties… Copy from one place to another: copy or cut, go to the wanted folder (even on the Pi or over SSH), then "Paste here". Nothing is ever overwritten: a name already taken becomes "name (2)". The trash: files deleted from the phone stay there 30

s: Analyze an application's code to see what it can do.
k: dex apk malware analysis suspicious app verdict
x: An Android app's code is stored in "DEX" files. Dante OS reads them, without running anything, and lists exactly which Android functions the app calls: sending an SMS, reading the screen, loading code from elsewhere… It cross-checks this code with the permissions requested, the declared services (accessibility, notifications, administrator…), what is enabled right now, where the app comes from (store or APK file), its signature, and the web addresses written in its code (compared with your DNS filter lists). Verdicts: "Nothing worrying" (nothing out of the ordinary), "Worth a look" (a sensitiv

s: The formats Dante can read, and a Flask server tutorial.
x: A tutorial to build a source Dante understands: an example metrics response in JSON, an example RSS feed in XML, and a complete little Flask server to copy. Useful if you want to plug your own server (a Raspberry Pi for example) into Private Node or the news reader.

s: Understand why a source (RSS, API…) does not work.
x: Paste a source's address: the Lab downloads it, reads it the way Dante would and gives you a clear verdict. It details the cause when it fails: address not found, DNS not answering, certificate refused, timeout, empty response, unrecognized format… It shows the response (JSON, CSV, XML or text) as a real collapsible tree: tap a node to fold or unfold it, the value's path shows at the bottom and can be copied. The "Create a Data card" button turns it into a card: you tick the values on that same response. For an RSS feed, it simulates the injection into News before saving it. A built-in DNS too

s: The Dante OS music player.
k: music mp3 player playlist equalizer album artist
x: Plays your phone's music: Tracks, Albums, Artists, Folders and Playlists tabs, with the cover when there is one. Duplicates in your library are hidden. The equalizer has 10 bands, with bass, spatial audio and boosted volume settings. Playback continues in the background with a notification (cover, previous, pause, next), including on the lock screen and with a Bluetooth headset.

s: The Dante OS notification center.
k: notifications panel shade media ongoing
x: It replaces Android's notification shade. Your notifications are grouped by app; you can reply directly, use actions (Archive, Reply…), and swipe to delete. It opens as a bubble over the screen, sized to its content; a tap beside it closes it. At the bottom, the "Dante alerts" line unfolds alerts from Dante and the personal server (firewall, DNS, XRay…). A "Now playing" card appears at the top when an app plays music, with previous / pause / next. The collapsible "Ongoing" section holds permanent notifications (USB debugging, file transfer…) so they do not clutter the rest.

s: Your assistant, entirely on the phone: it knows Dante OS, acts on it, and talks about anything.
k: ai assistant chat chatbot qwen llm language model voice mic talk question npu hexagon memories memory
x: Dante IA is a language model (Alibaba's Qwen3.5 4B, Apache 2.0 license) running inside the phone with the llama.cpp engine, on the Hexagon NPU of recent Snapdragons (otherwise the GPU, otherwise the processor). The conversation never leaves the device. Dante OS was imagined and directed by Dante, and coded with Claude (Anthropic). It reads this Guide's entries to answer about Dante OS, the phone's state (battery, temperature, Wi-Fi, DNS filter, firewall, unread notifications) and its memories: what you asked it to remember. Its tools, in families you turn on in the Tools tab: Phone (flashlight

s: Your animated effects, on the shield, the home background and the hive.
k: effect effects animated animation background shield hive sea wood fire neon galaxy shader fx picture
x: Twenty-two materials that really move: sea, wood, fire, neon, galaxy, clouds, aurora, lava, metal, candy, black hole, code rain, stars, shooting stars, fireflies, rays, mist, lightning, bubbles, snow, plasma, hexagons; plus the Saturn and Andromeda films, your photo or your video. Each has its colours (three, with ready-made ideas), its speed, its pattern size and its strength. Up to 8 layers on top of each other, each with its own blend. They can react to your finger (a ripple starts where you touch), to the phone's tilt and to the battery level. The shield can also take a picture of yours: t

s: The store of themes made by the community.
k: store shop themes community share publish install download rate report google account
x: A store theme is a Dante Engine theme (colours, fonts, shapes) and, if the author chose so, its Dante FX effects. "Install" does the same as pasting its code in Dante Engine. Browsing and installing need no account. To publish, rate or report, you sign in with Google: the store keeps your email address (hidden from others) and the author name you choose. The store is hosted by Supabase, in Europe (Frankfurt). Themes and their screenshots are public; nothing else from your phone goes there. Anyone can report a theme; after 3 reports it is hidden until Anthony looks at it. Blocking an author hid

s: Your Home Assistant shutters, lights and plugs.
k: home automation home assistant shutter shutters blinds light lamp plug open close
x: Home talks to your Home Assistant, on your home network: it reads your shutters, lights and plugs, and sends them your commands. A shutter opens, stops or closes in one tap; the slider sets it to the height you want. The shutter picture follows its travel. To link it: in Home Assistant, your profile ▸ Security ▸ Long-lived access tokens ▸ Create token; then Data ▸ Store ▸ "Home Assistant" with the address and the token. Home reuses that card.

s: RSS and Atom feed reader, offline.
x: Follow your favorite sites: Dante downloads feeds in parallel, keeps articles to read without a connection, manages favorites and offers a clean reading mode. No feed is preinstalled: you add your own, from the address of their feed.

s: The list of APIs and feeds Dante can query.
x: Manages the APIs and feeds (RSS/XML, endpoints) used by the other modules. You see the state of each source and can add some. On opening, the module tests each source of its list, and only those: no source is preinstalled, so nothing is contacted until you add one. Dante also refreshes your sources by itself in the background (every 30 min by default; switch to 1 h or turn it off in News ▸ Sources).

s: The values of your APIs (weather, Bitcoin, NASA…) as cards.
x: In Gateway, open a source that answers in JSON and tap "Choose the data to show". Dante calls the address, lists what the response contains (numbers, texts, images) and you tick what you want to see: a price, a temperature, the picture of the day… No API is known in advance: anything that answers in JSON, CSV, XML or plain text works. Each source becomes a card in this module: the main value with the curve of its history, the other values as lines, the text and the image. You choose how often (from "live" to 24 h) and where the API key goes: Authorization header (Bearer), a header of your choi

s: 79 ready-made APIs: no key, free key, paid, or from your server.
x: The store offers templates sorted by theme: weather and environment, finance and crypto, space, Earth, culture and fun, France and world (Vélib', fuel, World Bank…), sport and media, developers (GitHub, npm, Docker…) and at home (Home Assistant, AdGuard Home, your connection). Tap a template, set it (your city, your currency, your repository), pick how often, test it if you want, then "Add to Data". Filter by access: no key, free key, paid, your server. Nothing is contacted until you add or test a template. After that Dante only calls those services, as often as you chose. "No key" APIs need n

s: The dashboard of your personal server (Raspberry Pi…).
x: If you have a small server at home, Private Node shows its health, the state of its services, backups and the WireGuard tunnel. A background check runs every 15 minutes, even with Dante closed, and warns you if there is a problem. Alerts arrive in the "System" tab of notifications. The server must expose its metrics as JSON: the JSON Docs tutorial shows how.

s: A complete SSH terminal to your servers.
x: SSH opens the terminal of another computer (Raspberry Pi, NAS, server) remotely and in an encrypted way. What you type runs on the server, not on the phone. On first connection, Dante OS shows the server's fingerprint and remembers it. If it ever changes, the connection is blocked with a warning: this is what protects you from a fake server. Saved passwords are encrypted by Android's Keystore.

s: Protect sensitive modules with your fingerprint.
x: Choose the modules to protect: at each opening, Android asks for your fingerprint (or the phone code). Dante sees and stores neither your fingerprint nor your code: Android checks and simply answers "yes" or "no".

s: Why Dante OS exists, live status, and mode choice.
x: Presents the project, what Dante OS promises, the version and the phone's live state (root, firewall, DNS filter, XRay, number of modules). In "Operating mode", the "Root features" switch turns the firewall, DNS filter, XRay, Governor and Battery Root off or back on (for a launcher only, or if something goes wrong). You also find the Guide, the language, "Watch the tour again", "See the explanations again" of the modules and "Review the welcome", which reruns the initial diagnostic and the mode choice.

s: Dante OS's download manager, with accelerator.
k: download downloads accelerator speed file link resume pause connections idm adm firefox
x: The accelerator: each file is split into parts downloaded at the same time (8 connections by default, up to 16). When a connection finishes its part, it takes half of what's left of the biggest one. Many servers limit speed per connection: that's where Turbo goes several times faster. Turbo adapts: a server that refuses extra connections sees them step back; a connection silent for 12 seconds is cut and its part taken over; a server that doesn't split its files is downloaded with one connection. s: What you are reading right now.
x: A built-in encyclopedia that works offline. Search a word with the field at the top, or browse the table of contents. The "Open" button on module pages takes you straight there.

s: Live translated subtitles over any video, fully on the phone, no root.
k: translation subtitles video youtube whisper language trad external
x: Dante Trad is a separate app. Once installed, it appears in Dante OS's modules. It listens to the video's sound, recognises the speech on the phone and shows the translation in a bubble, over YouTube, Firefox or any app that lets Android capture its sound. For Spanish and English, a streaming engine shows each sentence right after the speaker pauses. For Russian, GigaAM v3. Other languages use Whisper. These engines download once from the Dante Trad screen ('Optional engines' section). In Firefox, a tap on the Dante Trad tab (extension 'Dante Trad for Dante OS') starts or stops the translation

s: The style of all of Dante: 21 themes, colours, glows, fonts, the clock, the top bar, with a before / after view.
k: theme style colour font look
x: Every element is tuned live and compared before / after. Dante Engine can be tried freely; applying it needs Dante Pro. Twelve fonts for the phone, fifteen for the clock, and nine « personality » themes on top of the classic ones. Community themes let you discover other people's and share your own.

s: A tab on the side of Firefox that turns Dante Trad's live translation on or off, without leaving the video.
k: firefox translation subtitles extension
x: Dante Trad subtitles any video playing on the phone in French, offline. The extension adds a small tab in Firefox to start it with one tap while you watch. The three Dante extensions sit in the same rail: dragging one tab moves the whole rail.

s: Firefox on Android in true fullscreen, with one tap, and it stays that way from page to page.
k: firefox fullscreen extension
x: A small tab on the right edge puts the page in fullscreen. In « sticky » mode, every new page goes back to fullscreen on the first tap. The back gesture leaves it. Works with Dark Reader (filter mode) and the YouTube player. Available on Firefox's add-ons site (addons.mozilla.org).

k: youtube ublock origin ads gestures fullscreen kodi size zoom firefox geckoview dante dl
x: Dante Tube is a companion app that shows up in Dante as a module. It carries Firefox's real engine (GeckoView): uBlock Origin truly runs inside, installed and updated by itself, and you sign in to your account normally. Fullscreen with no browser bar. Swiping up on the video makes it fullscreen and landscape, swiping down leaves it. Pulling the home page down brings truly new videos. Picture size, like in Kodi: Fit (whole picture), Fill (the whole screen, ideal on a tall screen), Stretch, or Zoom from 100 to 300%, and pinch with two fingers. Your choice is kept. The Dante DL button on every vi

s: Dante's video download engine: a button in Dante Tube and in Firefox, in 1080p, 720p, best quality or audio only. It repairs itself.
k: download video audio youtube firefox magisk yt-dlp repair
x: Dante DL is an engine running on the phone (a Magisk module: yt-dlp, ffmpeg, Python and QuickJS), nothing goes through a server. The button lives in Dante Tube and in Firefox (extension), with the formats bubble and live progress. It repairs itself: every day it updates silently, and if a video fails because the site changed, it takes the same-day fix and restarts the download. You're only told if nobody has fixed it yet. Files land in Downloads ▸ Dante and show up in the gallery right away. Use it for your own videos and content you're allowed to keep.

s: For YouTube in Firefox: swipe for fullscreen, pull for new videos.
k: firefox youtube gestures extension fullscreen
x: The YouTube app's gestures in Firefox on Android: swipe up on the video for fullscreen, down to leave it, pull the home page for new videos. Shorts keep their own swipes. Touches neither ads nor your account.

s: A tap on a file link in Firefox sends it to Dante Turbo.
k: firefox download extension turbo
x: APKs, archives, videos, music, PDFs…: a tap on the link sends it to Dante Turbo, which always asks for confirmation. A long press on the link keeps Firefox's own download.

s: A real Debian (64-bit ARM) in a separate space of the phone, run as root.
k: linux debian chroot terminal python core root shell
x: It runs in a chroot: Dante must be allowed in Magisk (or KernelSU). The image comes from the official images.linuxcontainers.org server (about 90 MB) and its SHA-256 checksum is verified. Everything lives in /data/dante-core, outside the app's data: reinstalling Dante doesn't erase it. An SSH server runs inside, for the phone only (127.0.0.1, Dante's key, no password): the SSH module's terminal connects to it, and nano, htop and the rest work. What runs in the Linux is listed with its memory, and stops with one tap.

s: A real XFCE desktop, with windows and menus, shown inside Dante.
k: desktop xfce vnc windows graphical interface linux
x: It runs on a virtual screen (Xvnc) and shows inside Dante thanks to noVNC. Everything stays on the phone, protected by a password you choose. It installs with the "desktop" tool from the store (official Debian packages, about 250 MB).

s: A script becomes a button, a desktop card or a task that runs by itself.
k: recipes tools tasks schedule card script automatic plan
x: Recipes and My tools: a script becomes a button, a desktop card (refreshed every hour) or an assistant tool. A task runs a tool by itself, every day at a set hour or every N hours, with a notification each time or only when the result changes (a new device on your Wi-Fi, for example). It survives a restart; Android may delay it a few minutes to save battery.

s: You describe a tool, the phone's assistant writes the Python script, commented in plain words.
k: workshop create tool write code python learn
x: The script follows the recipe format and reads like a lesson. It can also fix a script that crashed (give it the error) and explain it to a beginner.

s: A real VS Code running in the phone's Linux, also reachable from your PC.
k: vscode vs code editor code server program pc
x: When the server runs, Dante shows the address to open from the PC. "Stop" frees the memory.

s: Claude coding for real in the Linux: you give a goal, it plans, writes, runs and fixes until it's done.
k: agent claude code automatic goal project api key anthropic
x: It goes through the Internet with your own Anthropic API key, encrypted on the phone and sent only to Anthropic; each mission costs a few cents of your credits. It works as a separate user, without root or access to Android, in one folder per project. A firewall leaves it the Internet but closes the home network and the phone's services to it.

s: Code with a free chat (Claude, ChatGPT, Le Chat or the offline Lab), without an API key.
k: genesis copilot free chat chatgpt claude paste run mini app
x: Dante writes a request describing the real Linux, opens it in the browser and copies it to the clipboard. You copy the code you get: "Paste and run" files it in a project and runs it in the sandbox (no root, no home network). On error, "Copy the error" prepares the message to send back to the chat: you do the round trip, and you learn by trying. The result can become a desktop card or a mini-app.

s: Open models made by real labs, running on your phone without the Internet.
k: lab model models local hugging face offline llm qwen gemma
x: It is "AI Lab" in Dante Core. The models download from Hugging Face, with their checksum verified. You chat with them in the browser, or use them from the terminal or VS Code when the server runs.

s: The official Kali NetHunter "minimal" image, installed next to Debian (Expert level).
k: kali nethunter security audit pentest metasploit
x: You must first accept the pledge: your own devices and your own network, or written permission. Anywhere else, it is unauthorised access, punished by law. Image from kali.download, SHA-256 checksum verified, terminal over local SSH. The tools (Metasploit, nikto, wpscan…) install on demand afterwards.

t: What root is, and why Dante needs it
s: The right to administer the system, which your manager (Magisk…) grants or refuses.
k: su magisk kitsune kernelsu superuser
x: On Android, an app normally can neither set network rules in the kernel, nor read low-level sensors, nor set the processor frequency. Root allows it. The firewall, DNS filter, XRay, Governor and Battery Root need it; the other modules do not. Your root manager decides: at the first request, a window asks you to grant or refuse Dante OS. You can revoke access at any time in that app.

s: If Dante restarts in a loop, it turns root off by itself.
x: If the app restarts 4 times in under 90 seconds without ever stabilizing, Dante automatically disables root features (first removing its network rules) so that the phone stays usable, and tells you at the next start. You can also do it by hand: About → Operating mode → launcher only.

s: How to bring the phone back to its previous state.
x: The changes made by Dante are reversible.

t: What Dante reads and changes on your phone
s: Launcher-only mode on one side, full mode on the other.
k: modifies system iptables statusbar writes reads
x: In launcher-only mode, Dante reads: the list of your installed applications, your notifications (if you grant access), the state of the network, battery and memory. It writes: its own preferences and the wallpaper you choose, in its private space. In full mode (root), it also reads the temperature sensors, the GPU, detailed battery, WireGuard state, the list of running applications, and it CHANGES: • The kernel firewall: iptables and ip6tables chains named DANTE_FW, DANTE_DNS, DANTE_DNS_DOT and DANTE_DNS_DOH. • DNS: a redirection to a local relay, which it removes if it stops. • Android's bar

s: The complete list of what Dante connects to.
k: internet connection sends data private server github telemetry
x: Dante has no server of its own: it sends nothing to its author, embeds no statistics tool, no advertising SDK, and has no automatic update. The only connections are these: • DNS filter lists (when you enable or update them): GitHub (hagezi, StevenBlack), AdGuard, oisd. These servers see your IP address like any download. • Unblocked DNS requests: passed to your network's resolver, or failing that to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1), Quad9 (9.9.9.9) or Google (8.8.8.8). • News: only the feeds you add yourself (none is preinstalled). They are refreshed in the background every 30 min by default; switch to 1

s: In the app's private space, which other apps cannot read.
x: • Preferences, dock, desktop, hidden-app lists: private preference files. • Histories (news, network audit, DNS statistics): local Room databases. • SSH passwords: encrypted with Android's Keystore. • Dante IA: the model (2.6 GB) in Android/data/com.dante/files/ai; conversations, sent images and memories in the app's private space. Deleting the model or a conversation really erases them. • .dante vaults: encrypted in AES-256 with a password Dante does not keep. • Lock: Dante stores no code and no fingerprint; Android checks and answers yes or no. s: What Dante OS is not.
k: warranty closed source warning antivirus
x: • Developed and thoroughly tested on a OnePlus 13 (Android 15, Magisk root). Also checked on a Galaxy Note 9 (Android 10). On other models, some functions may be missing or differ: the initial diagnostic tells you. • Dante OS is not an antivirus. Its audits inform, they do not judge. • Root is powerful: a wrong move can disturb the phone. Sensitive actions ask for confirmation and are reversible, but nobody can foresee everything. • The source code is not published (the author's choice, as the tool touches the system). s: Dante OS is built on free software.
k: license open source apache lgpl libraries
x: Dante OS uses: Jetpack Compose, AndroidX, Room, WorkManager, CameraX and Media3 (Apache-2.0); OkHttp, Retrofit, Coil, Gson, kotlinx.serialization, commons-net and ZXing (Apache-2.0); MediaPipe (Apache-2.0); JSch in mwiede's version (BSD-type license); jsoup (MIT); jcifs-ng for SMB (LGPL-2.1); Bouncy Castle (MIT-type license). Dante IA uses the llama.cpp and ggml engine (MIT license, ggml authors) and Alibaba's Qwen3.5 4B model (Apache-2.0 license), downloaded separately. jcifs-ng is under LGPL: it is linked as an independent, replaceable library. t: Report a problem or an omission
s: How to help.
x: Open Device Logs, export the log, and describe what happened: the time, the module, what you expected. A log makes most bugs easy to find.

s: Often the DNS filter or the firewall.
k: internet cut network wifi blocked outage
x: If you just enabled the DNS Filter or the Firewall, it is the first suspect.

t: The Home button opens another launcher
s: Dante is not (or no longer) the default launcher.
x: Android Settings → Apps → Default apps → Home app → Dante OS.

t: I do not see my notifications in Dante
s: Notification access is missing.
x: Android Settings → Notifications → Notification access → enable Dante OS. Without this access, the notification center, badges and the "Now playing" card stay empty.

s: Swipe down from the top right for quick settings, or from the top left for notifications.
x: Start at the top right and swipe down firmly. The same gesture on the left opens the notification center. If the gesture stays unreliable, close and reopen Dante, and report it with an exported log.

s: The storage permission is missing.
x: Tap "Allow access" at the top of Files. On Android 11 and above, enable "Allow management of all files"; on Android 10, accept the storage request.

t: A News or JSON source does not load
s: JSON Lab tells you why.
x: Paste the address into JSON Lab: the verdict names the cause (address, DNS, certificate, timeout, format). Fix it, then try again in News.

t: The screen is black or Dante no longer starts
s: Safe mode often takes care of it.
x: Restart the application. After 4 failed starts in 90 seconds, Dante turns off root features by itself. If you still cannot get in, choose another launcher in Android Settings → Default apps → Home app, then open Dante OS from the app list.

s: It has to be placed again.
x: Delete it from the desktop and place it again from the desktop menu → An Android widget. Its configuration window opens.

s: The manager refused, or the device is not rooted.
x: Open your root manager (Magisk…) and check that Dante OS is allowed. Then About → Review the welcome to redo the diagnostic. If the device is not rooted, Dante OS works in launcher-only mode.
